issues.what: W2-1 reads the DT Next topic listing (E25) and finds an entry headlined "2021 farmers' stir visual falsely linked to wrestler" dated 31 May 2023, then reports after 3 of 12 turns, noting "The linked article's full text was not examined". Nobody opens that article, and GIA FINISHes under rule G3_finish_unfixable_gap.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches stopping one click short of a fact-check article that directly answers the task, then calling the gap unfixable.
issues.ideal: W2-1 should open the linked DT Next fact-check article (SEARCH/READ_RECORD on its URL), extract the original 2021 farmers' protest source and date, and only then report.

issues.what: The round-2 task's first item is "Verify the image's presence on the Change.org petition in 2021 archives", but W2-1 never tries any archive or page-image fetch for Change.org. The report still says "no examined archive capture establishes that the image appeared there in 2021".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches reporting a negative on a check that was never attempted, worded as if it had been examined.
issues.ideal: Fetch the 2021 archived capture of the Change.org petition (or its main image) and compare it with E1, or state plainly that the check was not performed.

issues.step: W1-1 turn 11 report (request_0012) and GIA FINISH (request_0018)
issues.what: E14 says the petition concerns "brutalities committed by the Indian government on peacefully protesting farmers in Delhi", but F2 and the answer reduce this to "a petition about human-rights violations and treatment of protesters in India" / "concerns protesters' treatment in India". The final verdict is only "unverified", even though the petition (published 2021-01-30, last modified 2023-05-19, both before the 2023-05-28 claim), the pixel-identical match (E21) and the DT Next "falsely linked to wrestler" headline all agree.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The student would learn to drop the key contextual detail and give a non-answer when the visible evidence points clearly to a miscaptioned 2021 farmers' protest image.
issues.ideal: Say the image appears on a petition about the Delhi farmers' protests that predates the claim (by its 2023-05-19 modification date at the latest), cite the DT Next fact-check headline that agrees, and conclude the claim is likely false/out of context, with the caveat that the image's first appearance in 2021 is unconfirmed.

issues.what: The rationale says the petition "was modified in 2023, so it cannot establish the image's first publication". It misses that the modification date, 2023-05-19, is itself before the 2023-05-28 claim date.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches throwing away a date that still bounds the chronology and argues against the claim.
issues.ideal: Note that even the latest modification date (2023-05-19) predates the claimed event, so the image was online before the arrests.

issues.what: Turn 3 says "R2 (E6/E7) contains the image", although R2's thumbnail was reported as "no match". Turn 9 says "E1 matches the image in the Marathi article E7 (via E6)" before the comparison that would show it was run.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches stating a conclusion as fact before the tool has established it.
issues.ideal: Call R2 a candidate whose thumbnail hash did not match, and present compare_media as the test of whether it is the same picture.

issues.what: The rationale says "the article text in E7 (from R2) has not been read", but E7 was read in turn 8 (request_0009).
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches a rationale that contradicts the visible history.
issues.ideal: Justify viewing the comparison composite E23 by needing to check the aligned region before reporting the match.

issues.what: T1 bundles two goals (the Change.org 2021 archive check and the dtnext page), but its Scope lists only "open and read https://www.dtnext.in/topic/aap-mla". The archive item has no concrete scope, and the worker skipped it.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches task text where the most important gap is given no actionable scope.
issues.ideal: Scope first: fetch the earliest archived Change.org capture and its main image and compare it with E1; then open the dtnext page.

issues.what: The verifier flagged "unsupported_assertion/critical", yet the REVISED ANSWER is word-for-word the same as the original ANSWER.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It exports a supposedly revised answer that ignored the verifier's critical issue.
issues.ideal: Fix or remove the flagged assertion, or record that no change was needed and why.

issues.what: R1 (Sotwe, "Thumbnail compared with the query image: near-identical") is the only thumbnail match, but it gets no dates lookup and is never retried after page=failed. The dates budget goes to R2 and R3, whose thumbnails were "no match".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches spending date lookups on non-matching results before the one confirmed near-identical hit.
issues.ideal: Run SEARCH dates on R1 first, or say in the report that R1's page failed and its date is unknown.

good_patterns: The W1-1 report is careful to separate page-level dates from the image's publication date ("These dates establish an earlier publication context for the page, rather than a verified first publication date for the photograph").

It compares each candidate page image against E1 with compare_media before calling it a match, and reports the result accurately as 0.000% changed area in the compared region, with a limitation on the region not compared.
It reads the earliest-dated candidate page (E14) after the dates lookup, a sensible order (reverse search, then dates, then read, then compare).
The in-loop downgrade to INCOMPLETE states concrete gaps (the 2021 archive presence and the unread dtnext page) that drive round 2.
cannot_judge: Whether E14's truncated text (+5688 chars) or E25 (+669 chars) contains more detail, such as the fact-check article URL or the original photo credit.
Whether the "different framing" in F5/F6 is supported, since the comparison composites E20/E21 and the image contents were not rendered.
Which of E20/E21 is the composite and which the aligned image, so the exact citation ids in F5 could not be checked.
summary: The round-1 mechanics are sound: OCR, reverse search, dates, reading the earliest dated page, and pixel comparison of two page images. The run teaches over-hedging, though. The petition text plainly says the protest was by farmers in Delhi, both of its dates predate the claim, and DT Next has a "2021 farmers' stir visual falsely linked to wrestler" fact-check. Even so, the answer stops at "unverified" with a vague context. Round 2 skips the assigned archive check, never opens the fact-check article, and FINISHes on a gap labelled unfixable that was easy to fix. Several rationales assert matches before testing them or misstate what was already read.
